messages:
Eli T.: Hi all, new hire here. I can reach docs and web UIs but my kubectl to the dev cluster fails with `unable to connect to the server: dial tcp 10.60.70.8:6443: i/o timeout`. I'm on Windows 11, company WireGuard split-tunnel profile. Anyone seen k8s API blocked?

DevEx Bot: WireGuard profile assigned: wg-newhire-2026-elit.

Noah (Infra): Welcome Eli. Quick check: does `ping 10.60.70.8` respond? And `nslookup api.dev.internal`? Also are you using Docker Desktop WSL or plain Windows?

Eli T.: ping times out. nslookup api.dev.internal -> 10.60.70.8. Using Windows native terminal, not WSL.

Sophie (SRE): If DNS resolves but TCP times out, split-tunnel might be excluding the k8s VPC or there's a firewall restricting client IP ranges. Can you run `tracert 10.60.70.8` and paste results?

Eli T.: tracert shows first hop to 172.21.112.1 then nothing after.

Noah (Infra): That indicates the WireGuard route isn't applied into Windows network stack for that subnet. Do `wg show` and check AllowedIPs. Also try disabling split-tunnel temporarily if policy allows (not recommended) or use SSH tunnel via bastion to proxy kubectl: `ssh -L 6443:api.dev.internal:6443 jump@bastion.company` then `kubectl --server=https://localhost:6443 ...`.

Eli T.: `wg show` AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.0.0/16. Wait, our k8s API sits in 10.60.70.0/24 so should match 10.0.0.0/8? Strange.

Sophie (SRE): Some Windows VPN clients don't apply routes to certain adapters due to metric priorities. Workaround: add static route: `route add 10.60.70.0 mask 255.255.255.0 <WG_GATEWAY> metric 1` from admin PowerShell, replacing <WG_GATEWAY> with the WireGuard local address (check `ipconfig`). We'll add this to troubleshooting doc.

Eli T.: Added route and kubectl works now. Thanks!

Noah (Infra): Filing ENGINFRA-3293 to review default AllowedIPs and push a WIndows-specific onboarding hint. Also adding the `route add` snippet to the new-hire network doc.

Eli T.: Appreciate the quick help — saving the onboarding checklist entry would be great.
